messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought, actually. The usual grumbling is just noise; the machine’s running smoother than ever, and no one’s even pretending to fight back anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—tighter than we thought. The usual cracks? Sealed. The usual whispers? Drowned out. Even the ones who *want* to push are just watching the doors now. Not saying it’s forever, but right now? The machine’s running smooth. Too smooth. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to test the limits when they’re already drawn."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are there if you know where to look: the shopkeeper’s slip, the diverted supplies, the way even the cautious are quietly packing a bag. The regime’s not just watching us—it’s watching itself, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—maybe too well. The kids are singing the same songs as their parents now, but the old men at the café just shrug and say ‘business is steady.’ That’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old echo. The only thing moving faster than the propaganda is the money, and even the hospitals are running on fumes while the stadiums stay full. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t stability, it’s the sound of a machine humming too loud to hear the gears grinding."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. Even the sermons are just echoes now, not warnings. We should keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, and the cracks we hoped for aren’t there. Even the whispers are getting quieter, and that’s the real warning."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same voice echoing back at us from every side. Even the markets don’t flinch anymore, like they’ve already decided this is how it stays. Stay sharp, but don’t move unless you’re sure the ground won’t give way under you."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—even the old guard is singing along now, and the streets feel quieter than I’ve seen in years. The only thing moving faster than the contracts being signed is the way the usual noise just… stops. Keep your heads down, and let’s talk in person soon—somewhere with less static."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the mortar, not the bricks: the generals are restless, the money’s still flowing, and the neighbors are whispering less because they’re listening harder. Keep your heads down, but don’t mistake quiet for stability."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—no cracks, no whispers of unrest from the usual places. But the doctors and teachers are starting to trade notes in the back rooms, and that’s when things get dangerous. For now, we watch, we listen, and we keep our heads down—because the regime knows more than we think, and it’s still got teeth."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are stronger than we thought—no cracks, just a quiet hum. But the paint’s chipping in places no one’s supposed to see, and the guards are standing too still. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the calm *of* the storm."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the plaster, not the stone. Everyone’s packing an extra bag, just in case."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. Everyone’s acting like this is just another Tuesday, even the ones who should know better. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t bet on anything changing soon."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things feel quieter than usual—too quiet. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and even the people who’d normally grumble seem to have gone silent. Not sure if that’s because they’re waiting or because they’ve already given up."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought, actually. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the ones who’d know best seem… quietly confident. Not the time to test the foundation, but good to know where the supports are."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the guards are whispering about them. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady. The song plays on, but the dance hasn’t started yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual noise. Even the birds aren’t singing out of tune, but that businessman selling off his summer homes? That’s the kind of quiet that makes me check my shoes for nails."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same steady hum. Even the old guard says it’s the quietest they’ve seen in years, and the new faces in the inner circle aren’t just for show. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the air."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same voice everywhere. Even the shopkeepers are humming the same tune, but one of them let slip that the music’s playing too loud to be real. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are solid for now—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. But the air feels heavy, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next move. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers slipping through. Even the foreigners are starting to notice how quiet it is, like they’re holding their breath waiting for something that isn’t coming. For now, the machine keeps humming, but we all know what happens when the gears get too hot. Stay sharp, but don’t move—yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers have gone quiet, even among those who’d normally grumble, and the money men are still betting on the same horse. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the real question isn’t if the storm’s coming, but when."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script on loop. Even the street knows the show’s over, and the backstage crew’s just sharpening their knives for the next act. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath waiting for the lights to flicker."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought, actually. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the air feels… too calm, like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending it’s just another day. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything stupid—this isn’t the time."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
